correctness.rationale: For all integers d>=2 and each fixed 0<theta<1, the Laplace transform of each common-shock coordinate simplifies exactly to 1/(1+s), giving entropy 1 for each margin. The conditional likelihood of the vector given W=JZ factors through the sample minimum M, so I(W;X)=I(W;M). Conditional independent exponential noises give h(X|W)=d(1+log q), while M=W+(q/d)E has the explicit normalized convolution density in the result. Hence TC=d log(1/q)+1+log(q/d)-h(M). The exact mixture-entropy identity implies TC=d log(1/q)-theta log(d/q)-H_b(theta)-theta delta+H(J|M), with 0<=delta<=log(1+q/d) by conditional entropy and maximum-entropy bounds. Threshold classification at M>d^(-1/2) bounds H(J|M) by binary entropy of a false-classification probability <=q exp(-sqrt(d)/q)+theta/sqrt(d), proving the three-term expansion and explicit remainder bound. The standalone scalar quadrature and mixture-entropy reproducer passed; finite numerical checks are not treated as infinite-dimensional proof.

originality.rationale: The 2023 multivariate Raftery copula and Bernoulli/common-exponential construction are expressly credited, as are general total-correlation and copula-entropy definitions. Primary full-text comparisons identified no exact scalar entropy reduction, dimension-dependent logarithmic correction or constant-order term in the originating homogeneous paper or its more general 2024 heterogeneous extension. Search results and related published scientific claims were compared by mathematical implication, not by title. These observations support a qualified originality assessment rather than an exhaustive priority certification.

value.rationale: The original multivariate Raftery paper analyzes moments, concordance and tails without identifying how whole-vector information dependence scales with dimension. Determining total correlation requires the full joint law and does not follow from pairwise dependence measures. The exact reduction from an arbitrary-dimensional KL calculation to one-dimensional sample-minimum entropy is structurally useful for evaluation; the coefficient -theta of log d and constant -H_b(theta) quantify an unexpected mixed discrete/continuous latent-shock penalty. Explicit uniform-in-d fixed-parameter error inequalities allow controlled finite-dimensional use. The invariant and asymptotic coefficients are motivated by high-dimensional dependence, not chosen ad hoc.
